**Status:** [WIP]

<!-- Derived from plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.spec.md (spec sections 13, 17, 18, 12.4-12.5).
     This is the tracker for the neatRacing voxel racer flagship demo. Phase/step/slice
     structure mirrors spec section 17 phases P1/P2/P3 1:1 with slice_ids kept verbatim
     so section 18 traceability holds without renumbering. Planning-only authoring pass:
     no src/, docs/, examples/, or scripts/ production edits. -->

## Scope

- Implement the neatRacing voxel racer per `plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.spec.md`:
  Phase 1 graphics engine + manual keyboard driving (AC-001..AC-024 + AC-040..AC-042),
  Phase 2 AI migration with NGE growth engine (AC-025..AC-034 + AC-043),
  Phase 3 polish + deprecation prep (AC-035..AC-039),
  Phase 4 AI-core integration (USER VERDICT 2026-11-07 — the plan is NOT complete:
  the AI core is missing; the Phase-2 [DONE] claims hold at the MODULE level only;
  Phase 4 re-opens AC-027..AC-034 + AC-043 in the LIVE lane and authors the NEW
  user-verdict ACs AC-100..AC-103; see the `## Phase-4 AUDIT` section).
- Planning-only pass in this instance: author full machine-readable step packets,
  register the plan, rebind the session, reindex RAG, prove gates. Execution is
  dispatched step-by-step to implementing/testing specialists after verification.
- Single source of truth for acceptance criteria and validation commands is the spec
  (section 13 ACs, section 12.5 conventions); this tracker binds each spec slice to its
  ACs, files, red-test notes, and validation commands.

## Mandates

- **Planning-only:** this authoring pass edits only `plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md`,
  `plans/README.md`, `plans/Roadmap.md`, `.vscode/mcp.json`, and RAG index artifacts.
- **Spec lock:** spec section 12 locked decisions register (LD) and resolved open
  questions are not reopened by the tracker. Deprecation prep is notices-only
  (LD-33); removal of `examples/racing_curriculum` is a separate user-confirmed
  workstream and out of scope.
- **Machine-readable packets:** every execution step carries a YAML packet with
  `expansion: slices`, `auto_expand: true`, and a `tdd_sequence` that MATCHES the
  slice roles the packet carries (`red-green` when the FIRST slice is a
  red-testing slice, `green-only` when the first slice is an implementing slice),
  and typed slices (slice_id / title / status / goal / estimate_hours /
  files_to_change / acceptance_criteria / parallelizable / dependencies) per the
  step-packet gate schema.
- **Slice discipline:** each slice is one atomic behavioral intent bound to spec
  section 17; at most 3 code files per slice (sibling `*.test.ts` files count;
  trivial one-line config registrations such as a package.json script line or a
  tsconfig include may accompany without counting); estimate_hours <= 4; at most
  5 slices per step - a step that needs a SIXTH slice is SPLIT into two steps
  and the split is recorded in the wave note, in the phase step list and in the
  plan tail (the at-most-5 limit is a MANDATE: a deviation is never recorded in
  its place, and a split NEVER defers a re-pin away from the production change
  that invalidated the pin).
- **Red-first:** every implementation slice carries `red_test` notes (the failing
  assertion to author first) honoring the spec RED -> IMPLEMENT -> GREEN rule; each
  step ends with a green-testing slice that runs the section 12.5 validation list.
- **Named constants:** tuning values use the named constants from the spec open
  questions patch (NEATRACING_FIXED_RENDER_HEIGHT, NEATRACING_MAX_BACKING_WIDTH,
  NEATRACING_AI_MIN_SESSION_LAPS, NEATRACING_EDITOR_UNDO_BUDGET_BYTES,
  NEATRACING_REBUILD_P95_BUDGET_MS, NEATRACING_ADAPTATION_TICK_BUDGET_MS, etc.).
- **Zero per-frame allocation (P9)** and **capacity limits preserved** (maxNodes 8000 /
  maxConnections 32000, AC-029) are standing constraints on all Phase 1/2 slices.
- **No deferred cleanup:** when a slice replaces an existing module or script, the old
  code is removed in the same slice.
- **No git:** agents never run git commands; all changes land via direct file edits.
- **Evidence:** gate runs are recorded in `## Latest validation evidence`; green-light
  recording is reserved for the separate verification instance.

### AC-087..AC-090 RE-DERIVATION (2026-10-27, verdict-4 + verdict-5, 01-planning AUTHOR)

**Scope of this subsection.** The author_handoff item 5 of the `verdict5-merged-gap-map` record: *keep AC-087..AC-090 semantics and re-derive their numeric pins from the equilibrium + the manual-mode rule*. The four SEMANTICS are unchanged (slide prominence with a recorded feel direction, a measurable traction signal, a no-regression ledger, and a user visual gate). The NUMERIC PINS are re-derived, because every pin that was written against the pre-wave model, against the AI-mode page, or against a transient reading is either vacuous or unreachable after the re-wiring. This subsection is the single home of the re-derivation; the row text above only points here.

**The two rules that drive every re-derived pin (the merged-map `acceptance_rules_for_the_author`):**

- **R-MANUAL (the measurement lane):** every slide, camera and traction measurement is taken with the page in **MANUAL** mode and the car **ON THE ROAD**. The ai-mode page is never acceptable evidence (R-M3). The page used to boot in AI mode (`INITIAL_RACE_MODE = MODE_OPTION_AI`, `examples/neatRacing/host/mode-selector.ts:63`), and the autopilot only crosses the `|steer| >= 0.5` engage cliff on **176 of 7200 ticks (2.44 %)** — so the AI page barely ever produces the slide the user is judging. The off-road excursion is the second mask: the demo track puts the car **OFF-ROAD at tick 280 at 82.3 m/s** (921 of 1200 ticks), where the `22.25 m/s` floor pins the car at `80.1 km/h` and the off-road deceleration is **32 : 1** the drift scrub — the slide is arithmetically erased. The re-wiring therefore starts with the two masks: the boot mode (Step 14P, slice `P1-drift-rewire-boot-mode`) and a ROAD-ONLY surface classification (Step 14P, slice `P1-drift-rewire-road-surface`).
- **R-EQUILIBRIUM (the deficit pin):** the speed deficit is pinned at the **EQUILIBRIUM 32.911 km/h** (the envelope audit), **never** at a transient 600-tick reading (which reads `32.555 km/h`). The repeat-offence in this plan has been to pin a transient; the re-derived contract waits for a convergence criterion and then measures.

**AC-087 (slide prominence) — semantics retained, pins re-derived.** The semantics are retained exactly: a **named** slide-prominence floor; the feel **direction decided and recorded in this plan before any production edit** (a bigger slide — decision D-11); the user-approved body-animation **shape** retained (the second-order pose spring with the steer-articulation term); and a sustained-slide contract. The re-derived pins:

1. The floor stays asserted on the **deterministic unit proxy** (`computeDriftSlideProxyRad(slipAngleRad)`), and the browser reading stays a loose **presence** observable (`driftFeelSlideProminence`) that is never numerically compared against a constant. (Unchanged — this pin was already correct.)
2. **The slide DEPTH becomes SPEED-PROPORTIONAL.** The measured defect is that the committed slide is the **same 0.45 rad at 5 m/s and at 89 m/s** (the envelope audit): the entry ramp is a fixed `3.5 rad/s` (speed-independent) and the clamp is reached in 8 ticks at every speed. The re-derived contract: the depth at the top speed is at least `0.45 rad` **and** the depth at a low speed is at most `0.20 rad` (the exact split is a RED decision, `P1-drift-law-red` / RED-2). This is the physics half of the user's "the tires should lose traction also proportionally to the speed".
3. The **sustained-slide window** is measured **on the road, in MANUAL mode** (the off-road lane pins the car at 80.1 km/h and masks the slide).
4. The **speed deficit** is pinned at the **equilibrium 32.911 km/h**, never at the transient.
5. The camera and the body read the **same published slip** (the one shared scalar), so the frame can never be internally inconsistent — a travel-locked camera with a crabbing body is the exact defect the audits forbid. The camera aim is the **travel heading published on the physics state** (the new named field `travelHeadingRad`), and the body yaw source is switched from the **committed** slip to the **published** slip (the call site `examples/neatRacing/physics/physics.step.service.ts:457`).
6. **The 3D VIEW must MOVE.** A new red contract (`P1-drift-rewire-red` / RED-4, and the W4b contract A12) asserts the **camera basis** — the look target and the forward vector — differs from the nose-aligned values by the travel divergence, and is **bit-identical to the pre-wave basis** when the published slip is zero. The assertion never targets the seam or a channel value: the A1–A11 contracts and all 43 fixture checks can pass with a **frozen** camera, which is the trap the F3 finding names.

**AC-088 (traction) — semantics retained, substance corrected.** The semantics are retained: the tire traction loss is a **measurable, non-degenerate** contract rather than a feel claim. The substance is corrected, because the old contract measured two things that are not traction at all:

| Old measured quantity | Why it is not a traction signal | Re-derived quantity |
|---|---|---|
| a **fixed-sun lighting band** (the tire gradient, G-V4) | it is a lighting term, not a friction term | the per-tire grip and the tire gradient are driven by the **published traction severity** |
| the **raw steer echo** (the front-wheel yaw, G-V5) | it echoes the input, not the physics | the front-wheel yaw is driven by the **physics state** |
| the **committed slip** (the crab, G-V3) | the traction law reads the **published** slip, so the two disagree | **one** shared scalar, published on the state as `tractionSeverity` |

The re-derived contract: the severity is a **named function of the speed and the published slip** (the user law S-2/S-3), published on the state, `0` on a straight line, `1` at the full slide, **monotonic** in the slide depth, and computed on the **post-traction `car.speed`** — the same basis the traction law uses (the F11 rule: the basis must match, or the camera and the tires disagree). **No consumer re-derives it**: the car pass, the HUD, the camera and the debug seam all read the same field.

**AC-089 (no regression) — preserve set retained, re-baselined set extended.** The **PRESERVE SET** is unchanged and is never relaxed: AC-047A..AC-047D (the AC-047D byte-identity is re-anchored on the **production serializer** — a stronger contract than the whole-object `JSON.stringify` pin), the determinism twin-runs, the straight-line exact zeros, the low-speed exact-zero gate, AC-078 and its tyre-follow tolerance, and the 24 non-drift fixture checks. The **RE-BASELINED SET** gains, each with exactly **one ledger row** whose single home is **this plan** (the pin, the old baseline, the new baseline, the **measured** value, the owner file):

### Derivation notes

1. **1:1 slice preservation:** spec section 17 slice_ids (P1-S1-A .. P3-S2-C) appear
   verbatim with their spec file lists and AC bindings; section 18 traceability holds
   without renumbering. The tracker adds one trailing green-testing slice per execution
   step (id `<spec-step>-green`, e.g. `P1-S1-green`) to host the section 12.5
   validation sweep; spec impl slices keep goal `implementing`.
2. **a/b step splits:** spec steps with 5 impl slices (P1-S3, P1-S4, P1-S6, P1-S7,
   P2-S3) are split into part 1 (A-C) and part 2 (D-E) sub-steps because a
   gate-conformant green-only step needs at least 2 and at most 5 slices and a
   trailing green-testing slice (5 impl + 1 green = 6 > 5). Spec slice_ids, file
   lists, and AC bindings are unchanged by the split.
3. **Uniform green-only tdd_sequence:** spec slices are RED -> IMPLEMENT -> GREEN
   atomic units; per-slice RED notes live in the slice `red_test` field so the
   gate-conformant step shape is uniformly `green-only` (all-but-last slices
   `implementing`, last slice `green-testing`).
4. **Planning ACs** use the AC-PLN-001..AC-PLN-005 prefix to avoid collision with the
   spec AC-001..AC-043 numbering.
5. **Dual-parser layout contract:** two parsers coexist and this tracker satisfies both.
   The step-packet GATE parses only the fenced YAML packets (heading-agnostic). The
   neataptic-workflow MCP additionally parses HEADINGS scoped to `## Implementation
phases`: `### Phase <N> — <Title> [STATUS]` (H3 + em-dash, terminated by a
   `## …validation gates…` H2) and `#### Step <N> — <Title> [STATUS]` (H4) inside the
   phase body; the active [WIP] step also carries `**Step objective:**` and
   `**Required validation:**` prose sections (backtick commands prefix-matching the
   YAML `validation` list). Keep this shape on every future step flip.
6. **Global step numbering:** the coverage backlog `Step` column uses global
   step numbers across phases — Phase 1 = 02-15 (Step 13 = P1-boot-glue
   wiring; Step 14 = browser composition, inserted between Step 13 and the
   exit check per the batch-102 integration-gap classification; Step 15 =
   editor editing-loop composition, inserted between Step 14 and the exit
   check per the batch-105 editing-loop scope correction, patch #2),
   Phase 2 = 16-20, Phase 3 = 21-22. Phase 2/3 rows were renumbered from
   the pre-insertion global sequence (batch 19 item 78 obs a), re-renumbered
   after the batch-102 Step 14 insertion, and re-renumbered again after the
   batch-105 Step 15 insertion (the batch-26 renumber precedent) so
   "13"/"14"/"15" bind uniquely to Phase 1 steps and Phase 2 starts at
   global 16.

## The ad-hoc audit — the retired side artifacts vs the spec of record and the USER's five verbatim directives

**AUDITED 2026-10-31 by the 01-planning (AUTHOR) instance. PLAN-ONLY: NO production code was edited, NO browser was opened, NO served-page or CDP evidence is claimed, and NO status was flipped. The browser lane stays WAIVED-not-passed.**

### A0. The method, the evidence classes and the verdict vocabulary

Six ad-hoc research artifacts and five side review artifacts were folded into the canonical tracker files on 2026-10-31. Folding is not adjudication: a folded finding is a CLAIM until it is checked against (a) the spec of record, (b) the tracker's own acceptance ledger, (c) the CURRENT code, and (d) the USER's five verbatim directives. This section is that check. It is written so that a later reader can tell, for every claim, whether it still stands.

**THE EVIDENCE CLASSES.** Every finding below carries the evidence class its own artifact assigned, and this audit preserves that class rather than upgrading it:

- **STATIC** — a code read. Proves the SHAPE of the code, never its runtime value.
- **MEASURED** — a number produced by running the code (a probe, a fixture, a unit test).
- **DERIVED** — a number computed from a measured constant by a closed-form argument.
- **NONE** — no runtime measurement was performed at all.

**THE VERDICT VOCABULARY.** Each row of the audit carries exactly one verdict:

| verdict | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **CLOSED** | the defect the finding describes is fixed in the CURRENT tree; the finding is history. |
| **COVERED (WAVE)** | a tracker criterion (AC-047..AC-099) owns the finding and carries it into a slice. |
| **COVERED (SPEC)** | a criterion of the spec of record (§13) owns the finding. |
| **STALE** | the finding's PREMISE no longer holds in the CURRENT tree, so the finding must not be re-read as a live defect. |
| **GAP** | NO criterion (spec or tracker) owns the finding. It is an un-owned defect. |
| **CONTRADICT** | an existing criterion or spec clause states the OPPOSITE of the finding; the criterion must be re-contracted, not merely extended. |
| **NON-FINDING** | the artifact's own evidence disproves the suspected defect. |
| **CAVEAT** | a limitation on the evidence, not a defect in the code. |

**THE ONE THING THIS AUDIT DID NOT DO.** It did not re-run the drift fixtures, the browser fixture, or any browser session. Every "MEASURED" row below is either (i) a number this audit reproduced with an independent esbuild-bundled probe, or (ii) a number quoted from the artifact that produced it, marked as such. Where this audit reproduced a number, the probe is named.

The USER's five directives are verbatim USER text and are carried into the ledger as AC-094..AC-098. This table is the audit's ANSWER to the USER's question "do the ad-hoc artifacts say anything about the five things I actually asked for?"

| 2 | "touching the edge teleports you to the middle of the track, I didn't asked for that, cars can go off track, but it goes slow, as if on sand" | AC-094 / Step 14W | B-1 R3 (the off-road floor masks the scrub), B-2 R4 (the off-road floor can MASK a drift defect), B-3 G-11 (the HUD advertises a control the boot mode ignores) | **COVERED (WAVE)**, but with a live coupling: the off-track surface and the drift measurement share a floor, so any NEW traction measurement must be taken ON ROAD. |
| 3 | "the 'drift' camera effect is terrible, too sensitive, snaps back horrible, doesn't look like drifting and it makes the camera tilt too much (cap at half or less) and too fast (much slower)" | AC-097 / Step 14X | B-1 B4 / L5 (the speed-blind tire and the speed-blind chase), B-5 G-M3 (the render bridge is bound to the nose and the camera cancels the drift by construction) | **COVERED (WAVE)**, and the underlying causes are now CLOSED (the speed-blindness is gone). |
| 4 | "track should be wider on corners on the outer part of the curve, to give space for the drift" | AC-095 / Step 14U, and AC-099 / Step 14U2 | **THE AABB RASTER UNCLIP** — and NOTHING else in the ad-hoc set touches it | **THE ONE OPEN, USER-VISIBLE DEFECT.** The widening is published and painted, but the RASTER drops the widened corner cells, so the outcome is invisible. It MASKS this directive. Measured in A5 and promoted into Step 14U2 (AC-099). |

**THE SUMMARY OF A3: of the five directives, ONE (directive 4) is attacked by an OPEN defect, ONE (directive 5) is attacked by two OPEN input-shape residues, ONE (directive 2) is attacked by a MEASUREMENT-BASE coupling, ONE (directive 3) has its causes closed, and ONE (directive 1) is not attacked by anything.**

### A4. The spec-of-record drift that the ad-hoc artifacts exposed

This is the part of the audit that the ad-hoc artifacts do NOT themselves state, and it is the reason the USER asked for the audit against the spec.

#### A4.1 The AC-LEDGER DRIFT — 53 criteria live only in the tracker

| ledger | its range | where the criteria's TEXT lives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the SPEC of record, `plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.spec.md` §13 (the acceptance-criteria register) | **AC-001..AC-046** | §13.1..§13.3 carry AC-001..AC-039 in the `- **id: AC-###** — …` bullet format; §13.4 carries AC-040..AC-046 |
| the SPEC's §5.2 drift amendment | a DANGLING `AC-047` reference | §5.2 names `AC-047` and the sub-labels `AC-047A..AC-047D` in prose; **there is NO §13 register row for AC-047** |
| the TRACKER's ledger (`plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md`) | **AC-001..AC-099** | the coverage-backlog table is a MAP (criterion → step → slices), not criterion text; the AC-094..AC-098 acceptance TEXTS live inside the step packets, and AC-047..AC-093's texts live in the AC-087..AC-090 re-derivation and in the per-step packets |

**CONSEQUENCE: AC-047..AC-099 — 53 criteria — EXIST ONLY IN THE TRACKER.** The spec of record does not know they exist.

**THE SPEC LOCK DOES NOT REOPEN THIS.** The mandate locks the spec's §12 LD register and the resolved open questions against the tracker; it does NOT extend the spec's §13 register, and it does NOT authorise the tracker to edit the spec (the tracker's editable set is the plan tracker, the plan README, the roadmap, the MCP config and the RAG index artifacts). **So this drift is RECORDED here and ROUTED — it is not silently reconciled, and it is not silently ignored.**

#### A4.2 The SUPERSEDED §5.2 drift amendment — the spec's named constants no longer describe the code

The spec's §5.2 arcade-drift amendment names six constants. REPRODUCED by this audit against the CURRENT tree:

| the spec's §5.2 constant | the spec's value | the CURRENT code | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `NEATRACING_DRIFT_MAX_SLIP_ANGLE_RAD` | π / 2 = 1.570796 | **0.45** (`drift.model.ts:102`) | **SUPERSEDED** |
| `NEATRACING_DRIFT_GRIP_FALLOFF_THRESHOLD_RAD` | 0.25 | **0.2** (`drift.model.ts:205`) | **SUPERSEDED** |
| `NEATRACING_DRIFT_GRIP_FALLOFF_RATE_PER_RAD` | 2.0 | 2 (`drift.model.ts:215`) | unchanged |
| `NEATRACING_DRIFT_MIN_GRIP_FACTOR` | 0.25 | **THE CONSTANT NO LONGER EXISTS** — the landed suite ASSERTS its absence (`examples/neatRacing/physics/drift.model.test.ts:951`) | **RETIRED** |
| `NEATRACING_DRIFT_COUNTERSTEER_RECOVERY_RATE_PER_S` | 4.0 | **NO LONGER EXISTS** (asserted absent at `drift.model.test.ts:923`) | **RETIRED** |
| `NEATRACING_DRIFT_LATERAL_GRIP_RATE_PER_S` | 6.0 | **NO LONGER EXISTS** (asserted absent at `drift.model.test.ts:921`) | **RETIRED** |

**AND THE ALGORITHM ITSELF IS SUPERSEDED.** The spec's §5.2 describes a lateral-velocity model (an `atan2` slip, a centrifugal-multiplier outward push, a grip-falloff factor, a countersteer recovery and a passive lateral decay) integrated in a six-step order. The landed model is a COMMITTED-SLIP channel with a speed-dependent depth budget, a momentum demand law, a speed-proportional turn rate and a re-arm token. **The spec's §5.2 is not a re-derivable pin — it is a description of a model that no longer exists.**

**THE VERDICT: CONTRADICT.** The spec of record and the shipped implementation disagree about the drift model's constants AND its algorithm. The tracker's AC-087..AC-090 re-derivation already re-derived the pins the spec still holds; the spec was never re-amended.

**THE ROUTING (and the reason this audit did not simply fix it):** re-amending the spec is a SPEC-OWNERSHIP workstream. The spec is OUTSIDE this tracker's editable set, and the USER's request here was to AUDIT, not to re-amend. So the finding is recorded, quoted and routed; it is NOT closed by this section.

### A5. The quantified raster-unclip measurement (the defect that MASKS directive 4)

**THE DEFECT, IN ONE PARAGRAPH.** `measureSegmentSpanAabb` (`examples/neatRacing/track/track.slabs.ts:300-318`) measures ONLY the CENTRELINE CHORD ENDPOINTS. `synthesizeTrackSlabLattice` (`:355-390`) derives `originX` / `cellsX` / `originZ` / `cellsZ` from that span. The PAINTED SURFACE is not the chord polygon but the union of per-chord CAPSULES (a strip of the published half-width around each chord segment), classified by `resolveSurfaceIndexAt` (`:193-240`). **Every capsule cell that falls OUTSIDE the centreline AABB is therefore NEVER RASTERIZED.** By contrast the tri-colour band paint's sampling window IS grown by the widest published `outerHalfWidthM` (`examples/neatRacing/track/road-edge.ts:480-493`), so the band OVERHANGS the clipped road slab. The public analytic classifier `classifyTrackSlabSurfaceAt` (`:487+`) is NOT clipped — only the RASTER is — which is why the defect is invisible to any probe that reads the classifier instead of the grid.

#### A5.1 The measurement (seed 42, layoutVersion 1, sizeBucket small, 6 chords, counter-clockwise, `outerSideSign = -1`)

Reproduced by this audit with an independent esbuild-bundled probe over the REAL generator, the REAL edge seam and the REAL rasterizer:

| the centreline polygon AABB (what the lattice is sized from) | x ∈ [-116.265, 134.662], world z ∈ [-109.707, 132.447] |
| the CURRENT raster lattice | originX -116.5, originZ -110, **503 × 485** cells (world x ≤ 135, world z ≤ 132.5) |
| ⇒ the lattice clips the painted surface | **on BOTH axes** |
| the clipping depth | **8.275 .. 9.989 m** in x and **8.784 .. 9.089 m** in world z (on all four sides) |
| the widest published half-width | **10.463159974601306 m** |
| the named grass apron (`TRACK_SLAB_GRASS_APRON_WIDTH_M`) | **3.0 m** |
| the GROWN lattice (the CENTRELINE AABB + the widest half-width + the apron, on every side) | originX -130, originZ **-123.5**, **557 × 539** cells (world x ≤ 148.5, world z ≤ 146.0) |
| ⇒ the grown lattice contains the capsule union | **on BOTH axes** |
| the dropped ROAD cells | **4,299 of 47,127 painted = 9.1 %** |

| the dropped GRASS cells | **4,078** |
| the worst dropped road cell | world z = **140.75** |

#### A5.2 The second seed — and the independent confirmation of the Step 14I record

The probe was re-run on **seed 0, layoutVersion 1, sizeBucket small**:

| quantity | the measured value |
| --- | --- |
| the CURRENT raster lattice | originX -120.5, originZ **-136.5**, 457 × 549 cells (world x ≤ 108, world z ≤ 138) |
| the capsule union | x ∈ [-130.210, 116.982], world z ∈ [-145.187, 145.483] |
| the dropped ROAD cells | **5,292 of 47,903 painted = 11.0 %** (plus 1,108 curb, 3,715 grass) |
| the GROWN lattice (the CENTRELINE AABB + the widest half-width + the apron, on every side) | originX -134, originZ **-150.0**, 511 × 603 — **contains the capsule union on both axes** |
| the band reach | the union reaches world z = -145.187, so about **6 m** of band lands near world z ≈ **-151.19** |

**THE STEP 14I RECORD AND THIS MEASUREMENT AGREE EXACTLY.** The Step 14I evidence entry states "the road raster ends at world z = -136.5 while the paint band now runs to z ≈ -152". The independent probe reproduces **originZ = -136.5** at seed 0 / small, and puts the band's reach at **z ≈ -151.19**, which is the same figure to the nearest metre. **The Step 14I note was not an approximation, and the defect it recorded is the defect this audit measured.**

#### A5.3 WHY the growth rule is provably sufficient, and why it is purely additive

- **SUFFICIENCY (a proof, not a measurement):** every capsule point lies within `h` of a chord; every chord lies inside the convex polygon AABB; so the capsule union is contained in the polygon AABB GROWN by `h` on every side. Growing by the WIDEST published half-width plus the named apron therefore contains road + curb + grass with margin. The measurement confirms it on both seeds.
- **ADDITIVITY (a proof, not a measurement):** `resolveSurfaceIndexAt` never reads the lattice extent. Growing the domain can only ADD painted cells; it can NEVER change an existing cell's label. The growth adds raster DOMAIN and NEVER adds road WIDTH.
- **THE AXIS-ALIGNED CONSEQUENCE:** a lattice is an axis-aligned RECTANGLE, so it cannot grow on "the side the outer widening actually occupies". The outer/inner distinction applies to the PROBE and to the WIDENING MEASUREMENT (against the LOOP-GLOBAL `outerSideSign` = -1 for this counter-clockwise loop), NEVER to the lattice rectangle.
- **THE GREEDY MESHER CAVEAT:** the greedy mesher may change the QUAD COUNT of the extended runs, which is why the re-pin slice exists in the packet.

#### A5.4 WHY the USER saw NO visible fix — and the three hypotheses that were TESTED AND REFUTED

The USER's report (recorded verbatim in the 2026-10-31 USER evidence entry in `## Latest validation evidence`) is that `npm run build:neatRacing` + `npm run dev:neatRacing` showed NO visible change. Three alternative explanations were tested against the CURRENT tree by this audit. **All three are refuted, which is what makes the raster unclip the surviving explanation.**

| hypothesis | the test | the result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the served bundle was STALE (the build output never reached the browser) | compare the two bundle copies, their mtimes and the source mtimes | **REFUTED.** The dev server REBUILDS its own copy from the current source at start (`buildDevBundles`, `examples/neatRacing/server/dev-server.ts:655-672`), writing `examples/neatRacing/assets/neatracing.bundle.js` at **12:52:14**. The 14U paint edits (`track.slabs.ts` 11:41:06, `road-edge.ts` 11:41:38) are OLDER than that build, so **the served bundle DID contain the fix.** The `docs/assets` copy (12:53:34) differs only because the `collision.utils.ts` B-1 memoization fix landed at 12:52:55, between the two writes. |
| the BROWSER CACHE served a stale bundle under the fixed `?v=20260928-1` | read the dev server's static response headers | **REFUTED.** Every static response carries `cache-control: no-store` (`dev-server.ts:889`). The cache-buster is cosmetic, and B-3's G-13 is a NON-FINDING. |
| the page BOOTED in `ai` mode, so the drift was never engaged | read the live boot default | **REFUTED.** `INITIAL_RACE_MODE = MODE_OPTION_MANUAL` (`mode-selector.ts:78`). (This one WAS true for the ad-hoc artifacts and is now stale — see A2.4 G-1.) |

**THE SURVIVING EXPLANATION: the bundle was correct, the code was correct, and the defect is that the RASTER NEVER PAINTED the widened corner cells in the first place.** 37.3 % of the widening band was never rasterized, so the mesh the USER was looking at was, by construction, unchanged.

**TWO SECOND-ORDER PROCESS HAZARDS THAT SURVIVE (neither is the cause):** (i) the dev-served bundle and the `build:neatRacing` bundle are TWO DIFFERENT ARTIFACTS, so a reader inspecting `docs/assets/` is not looking at what the dev server serves; (ii) the dev server's rebuild is FIRE-AND-FORGET and SILENT (`void import('esbuild').then(...).catch(() => undefined)`, `logLevel: 'silent'`), so a build failure is invisible and there is a startup window in which the PREVIOUS bundle is still on disk.

- **NO criterion was closed, re-scoped or flipped, and NO status was changed.** The AC-090 USER GATE stays OPEN.
- **THE AUDIT DOES NOT RE-OPEN THE SPEC'S §12 LD REGISTER** and does not re-litigate the AC-087..AC-090 re-derivation.
- **THE `GF-1..GF-16` GAME-FEEL DECISION ROWS WERE NOT AUDITED** — they live in the plan tail, not in the research file.
- **THE AUDIT IS A SNAPSHOT.** It was taken against the tree as of 2026-10-31. Because the ad-hoc artifacts themselves went stale within a single wave (A2.3, A2.4, A2.6), a reader MUST re-verify any row against the current code before acting on it.

**User instruction:** "crowd sprites look giant-sized; reduce sprite height to 1/2 current on right-world crowd billboards" (SPRITE-1). The report is the anchor user-bug-report-2026-10-23-sprite-scale at the end of this plan, raised during the same live-page review that PASSED the Step 14K user visual gate ("looking great").

**Step objective:** Halve the world size of the right-world crowd billboards so the spectators stop reading as giant-sized next to the car. The rendered world HEIGHT of every crowd billboard - the seated spectators, the team-colored inner-ring mechanics, the slow walkers and the standing off-bleacher spectators - becomes EXACTLY 1/2 of its pre-14L height, with the world WIDTH following the SAME factor so the square 192x192 px atlas frames keep their aspect ratio. The factor is ONE named exported constant, NEATRACING_PUBLIC_BILLBOARD_WORLD_SCALE = 0.5 in examples/neatRacing/track/public.sprite.ts, applied inside computeBillboardScale so the placement footprint and the rendered quad can never disagree; the meters-per-sprite-pixel constant stays 0.05 m/px, so a 192 px frame goes from 9.6 m tall to 4.8 m. The halving changes the GEOMETRY only: the crowd counts, the per-frame billboard budget, the camera-relative facing, the 1 m personal space and the atlas bound all stay exactly as they are (AC-077).

**Decision set (2026-10-23 planning amendment):**

- **D1 - placement:** Step 14L is inserted between Step 14K and Step 14G, so the document order equals the routing-chain order 14F -> 14J -> 14K -> 14L -> 14G -> 14H -> 14I -> 14E -> Step 15. The anchor asks for the step "inserted before Step 14E" and "ahead of Step 14G"; the 14K precedent (D1 of the 14K decision set) is followed - the new step is placed at the HEAD of the still-open chain, immediately before 14G, so the 14L/14G demotion-and-requeue pair is one adjacent swap. Step 14E stays the last audited step and its audit scope now includes 14L; Step 15 keeps 14L as a prerequisite.
- **D2 - the single active boundary:** Phase 1 may hold only ONE [WIP] step (mcp-plan-utils.mjs loadActivePlanContext). The anchor makes 14L the new active boundary, so 14L is opened as [WIP] and Step 14G is DEMOTED to [PLANNED] (the 14K demotion pattern). No 14G work is lost: all its slices are DONE automated-green and only the user drift-feel / body-yaw visual verdict plus fix-packet-P1-turn-drift-green-iteration-11 stay open, re-queued after 14L.
- **D3 - uniform factor, not a height-only factor:** the anchor says "reduce sprite HEIGHT to 1/2 current". A height-only factor would SQUASH the square 192x192 px atlas frames, so the world WIDTH follows the SAME 0.5 factor and the rendered HEIGHT is still exactly 1/2 of the previous height - the literal request is satisfied without distorting the art. The alternative (a width-only factor) would leave the height unchanged and would NOT satisfy the request. This is recorded as a non-blocking note for the user; the sprite ATLAS is not re-drawn and no new frames are authored.
- **D4 - one named lever, applied at the single choke point:** the factor lives in ONE exported constant, NEATRACING_PUBLIC_BILLBOARD_WORLD_SCALE = 0.5, and it is applied INSIDE computeBillboardScale (public.sprite.ts:705). That function is the only scale source for BOTH the placement footprint (billboardWorldHalfSize, public.sprite.ts:1843) and the rendered quad (buildBillboardUpload, right-world.pass.ts:887), so the two can never disagree. The module-private BILLBOARD_WORLD_SCALE = 1.0 is removed in the same slice, and the off-bleacher footprint probe at public.sprite.ts:1486-1489 is re-authored onto the named constant, because it currently reads the raw private constant and would otherwise diverge from the rendered size.
- **D5 - the duplicated meters-per-pixel twin is removed:** right-world.pass.ts:107 keeps a byte-for-byte copy of the public.sprite.ts meters-per-pixel constant (0.05). The constant is EXPORTED from public.sprite.ts and IMPORTED by the pass, and the local copy is deleted in the same slice (no deferred cleanup). Leaving two copies alive while introducing a third factor would create exactly the drift the step is meant to remove.
- **D6 - the AC-054 absolute clause is superseded, the RATIO clause is retained:** AC-054 required a billboard to render at the same world size as a same-world-size voxel. A uniform 0.5 factor breaks that absolute clause by design, while the perspective-parity RATIO clause (a distant sprite keeps the same relative size, because the shared focal/distance projection is untouched) stays green. The stale 1:1 assertions in public.sprite.test.ts are RE-AUTHORED in the slice that changes the constant, not deferred: the 1:1 test becomes a 1:2 test against the named constant, and the absolute same-world-size test becomes a named-constant-relative 1/2 assertion.
- **D7 - the personal space is NOT sprite-derived:** the 1 m personal space (NEATRACING_ROBOT_PERSONAL_SPACE_M in right-world.builder.ts) and the off-bleacher clearance (NEATRACING_PUBLIC_OFF_BLEACHER_PERSONAL_SPACE_CLEARANCE_M = 1 m - epsilon in public.sprite.ts) are FIXED constants. The halving makes the personal-space band MORE permissive (the sprites occupy less world area), which can only INCREASE the admitted crowd, never starve it - and the anchoring-capacity filter that governs the seated population is size-independent, so the 12-per-bleacher and 240-total counts are expected to stay exact. A RED guard asserts both, because a count drift must never be silently accepted.
- **D8 - distance independence is preserved:** computeBillboardScale keeps ignoring its distance argument. The perspective shrink of a distant crowd sprite stays the shared focal/distance projection, so the halving is a pure world-size change and not a second, competing per-distance scale (a per-distance factor would have broken the AC-054 RATIO contract and the projection parity with same-world-size voxels).
- **D9 - slice discipline:** four sequential slices, each within the <= 3 files and <= 4 h budget, strictly ordered because the slice files overlap: P1-sprite-scale-red-contracts (red-testing) -> P1-sprite-scale-world-factor (implementing, public.sprite.ts) -> P1-sprite-scale-render-quad (implementing, right-world.pass.ts) -> P1-sprite-scale-green (green-testing, trackers). The two implementation slices are SEPARATE so that the placement footprint and the rendered quad are never half-migrated by a single oversized edit, and each implementation slice owns the test file it changes.
- **D10 - green-light ownership:** this authoring instance does NOT grant the green light. A fresh 01-planning verification instance records the green light in the Latest validation evidence section before Step 14L enters execution; the authoring instance must not self-dispatch a patch cycle.

**Stop conditions:**

- **Done:** all four slices green; AC-077 proven by the focused suites and by the rendered-quad measurement; the AC-054 RATIO contract and the retained invariants re-asserted green; the visible-window smoke shows the crowd sprites at roughly human scale next to the car, still standing on the bleacher level, with the same counts and no atlas upload error; the coverage backlog, AC-PLN-003, README/Roadmap, and the handoff query updated.
- **Blocked:** a slice cannot meet its file or estimate budget, the halved footprint seats a spectator BELOW the bleacher surface or drops one to the ground, a crowd count drifts at any fixture seed, or the halving cannot be proven on the rendered quad - record the blocker in the Latest validation evidence section and escalate via 00.cross-tier-helper. Never lower the 1/2 factor, the 12-per-bleacher count, or the 1 m personal space silently, and never let the sprite size drive the personal space.

**Required validation:**

- `npm run jest:base -- --testPathPatterns="examples/neatRacing/track|examples/neatRacing/engine"`
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.neatRacing.json --noEmit`
- manual: `npm run build:neatRacing` + visible-window browser smoke on the served `/` page (the crowd sprites are visibly HALF their previous size, a seated spectator is about 4.8 m tall instead of 9.6 m and reads at roughly human scale next to the 1.2 m car, the seated spectators still stand ON the bleacher level, the seated count per bleacher is still 12, the off-bleacher walkers, standing spectators and team-colored mechanics are still present, the seated spectators still face TOWARD the car, and there is no WebGL atlas upload error)

  - slice_id: 'P1-drift-traction-loss'
    title: 'Tires actually lose traction proportionally during a full-speed drift'
    status: '[DONE 2026-10-23 — 04-implementing: the tires now ACTUALLY LOSE TRACTION proportionally during a full-speed drift — the hard grip floor NEATRACING_DRIFT_MIN_GRIP_FACTOR = 0.7 is REMOVED (no deferred cleanup: the constant AND the clamped computeGripFalloff helper it clamped are DELETED) and replaced by the proportional tire traction law computeTractionFactor(slipAngle, speedPercent) = 1/(1+demand)^2 with demand = max(0,|slip|-0.25)*GRIP_FALLOFF_RATE_PER_RAD*speedPercent, PLUS the NEW longitudinal traction term computeLongitudinalTractionLoss(slipAngle, speed, speedPercent) that the longitudinal integrator subtracts from the car speed (examples/neatRacing/physics/physics.step.service.ts, step 4b); MEASURED at the arcade top speed (89 m/s) under a sustained full-steer full-throttle turn: the OLD model held the WHOLE top speed (89.0 m/s) with the slip pinned at exactly 40.34 deg by the 0.7 floor, the NEW model settles at 57.5 m/s (207 km/h) with a 45.5 deg slip and only 0.345 of the grip left (a 65% loss vs. the old 30% cap); the slide stays BOUNDED (the linear law was MEASURED to run away to 89 deg of slip and spin the car, which is why the consumption saturates); the low-speed and straight-line behaviour is UNCHANGED (AC-047D) and the determinism is preserved; the visible-window smoke fixture gains the named check proportionalTractionLoss with its diagnostics; jest physics|car|host 11 suites / 166 tests PASS, jest car-pass lane 1 suite / 4 tests PASS, tsc exit 0, eslint exit 0, quality:folder exit 0, build:neatRacing exit 0; the consolidated slice-advancement gate passes 7/7 (severity FULL, specialistCount 1); full evidence in ## Latest validation evidence]'
    goal: implementing
    estimate_hours: 3
    files_to_change:
      - 'examples/neatRacing/physics/drift.model.ts'
      - 'examples/neatRacing/physics/drift.model.test.ts'
      - 'examples/neatRacing/physics/physics.step.service.ts'
      - 'examples/neatRacing/physics/physics.step.service.test.ts'
      - 'docs/browser-tests/scenarios/p1-turn-drift-green-smoke.html'
    boundary_extension_note: 'BOUNDARY EXTENSION (declared by 04-implementing, 2026-10-23): the slice was planned with THREE files, and the AC-079 defect text itself ("the falloff is applied as a DRAIN-RATE multiplier ... with NO longitudinal traction term at all") can only be closed if the longitudinal traction term is actually applied to the LONGITUDINAL speed - which is integrated in examples/neatRacing/physics/physics.step.service.ts (step 4b) and pinned in its sibling test. A longitudinal traction term that nothing consumes would be dead code (a no-deferred-cleanup violation) and would leave the reported defect open, because the tires would still hold the whole top speed through any turn. The extension is therefore NECESSARY, MINIMAL (2 extra files, +33/-2 lines in the service and +73 lines in its test) and MECHANICAL (the drift model keeps owning every traction formula; the service only consumes it); the AC-079 coverage-backlog row names the same three planned files and is superseded by this note.'
    acceptance_criteria:
      - 'AC-079: the effective grip falls PROPORTIONALLY to the drift demand during a full-speed turn instead of being clamped by the hard grip floor; the low-speed and straight-line behaviour stays undegraded (AC-047D); determinism is preserved; and the visible-window smoke fixture gains the named check proportionalTractionLoss'
    red_test:
      - 'RED: drift.model.test.ts fails before the hard grip floor is replaced by a proportional law - assert the measured grip at a high slip angle is strictly BELOW the full-grip value and scales monotonically with the slip angle, and the smoke fixture reports proportionalTractionLoss === false before the fix'

    dependencies:
      - 'P1-arcade-drift-model'
      - 'P1-arcade-drift-visual'
    validation_evidence:

      - '2026-10-23 `npm run jest:base -- --testPathPatterns="examples/neatRacing/engine/passes/car"` -> 1 suite / 4 tests PASS (the AC-047C/AC-078 pins are UNCHANGED - the user-approved drift body animation is not touched)'
      - '2026-10-23 `npx tsc -p tsconfig.neatRacing.json --noEmit` -> exit 0; `npx eslint` over the four changed TypeScript files -> exit 0; `npm run quality:folder` over examples/neatRacing/physics -> exit 0 (0 TS diagnostics, 0 ESLint errors, 53/53 exported symbols documented, 0 modules missing a sibling test); `npm run build:neatRacing` -> exit 0 (esbuild, 48 ms)'
      - '2026-10-23 MEASURED physics A/B (same rig, same input, the production change is the only delta): at the arcade top speed (89 m/s) with a sustained full-steer full-throttle turn the OLD model held 89.0 m/s (320 km/h) with the slip pinned at exactly 40.34 deg by the 0.7 floor, the NEW model settles at 57.5 m/s (207 km/h) with a 45.5 deg slip and 0.345 of the grip left; a straight-line full-throttle run still reaches the whole 89 m/s and the low-speed straight-line state is bit-identical (AC-047D)'

      - 'the AC-047D byte-identity pin is RE-ANCHORED on the PRODUCTION serializer (physics.step.service.test.ts, the serializeState helper at lines 72-73) instead of the retired createZeroDriftState helper, and the new state fields (committedSlip, turnSign) are all exactly 0 on a straight line at 10 m/s, so the byte-identity survives the new state shape'
      - 'the fixture lands the new COUNTERSTEER PHASE and the named checks: the phase sequence P0 (boot and mode switch), P1 (straight-line acceleration, the zero-pose phase), P2 (drift entry and hold), P3 (the countersteer catch, a genuine release-then-opposite-press - a keyup of KeyA followed by a keydown of KeyD, never a simultaneous press), P4 (the settle), P5 (the right-hand mirror) and P6 (the straight-line re-check) are appended after the existing W+A phase and BEFORE the checks object; the uTireGradient* value capture is added inside recordUniform (the four floats the fragment stage reads); the NEW named checks are driftFeelFarSidePop (the browser bound 1.0 deg to 6.0 deg), driftFeelSettles (at most 900 ms), driftFeelNoStuckOffset (|pose| at most 1.0 deg), driftFeelPoseRateBounded (at most 128 deg per s, frame-rate independent), driftFeelPoseEnvelope (at most the declared envelope plus 0.002 rad), driftFeelZeroStraightLineYaw (max |pose| exactly 0), driftFeelSlideProminence (at least 0.10 rad - this is ONE check; the red-contracts name driftSlideProminenceReachesFloor denotes the same check and the fixture-gate name wins), tireGradientMagnitudeIsNonDegenerate (bright is not dark, radius above 0, threshold inside (0, 1)), driftFeelModelIdentity (max |slip| at most 0.45 + 0.02, the catch discriminator) and driftGateSurvivesThreeConsecutiveFrames; the check COUNT is ASSERTED against the actual result.checks length and is NEVER assumed (31 existing plus 10 new is the EXPECTED total 41, and the assertion is against the ACTUAL length); the retained fixture thresholds are DISPOSITIONED ROW BY ROW by the NEXT criterion against the 14N rebaseline-risk coverage note D3.1 threshold ledger, so this packet carries NO blanket "the retained fixture invariants do NOT move" claim, and the retained 290 km/h TRACTION_LOSS_MAX_SPEED_KMH ceiling is NOT carried forward - it is REPLACED per D1.3'

    acceptance_criteria:
      - 'the drift model becomes the D1 stage model with a FIXED stage ORDER that is asserted - the integration artifact section 4.3 table enumerates EIGHT numbered stages (0-7), the arcade-refs merge text calls it the 7-stage model, and the packet records the TABLE (the authoritative enumeration): stage 0 the MIN_SPEED gate (inside stepDriftCommitment), stage 1 the commitment ramp with the ENTRY_RATE and EXIT_RATE (inside stepDriftCommitment), stage 2 the grip budget factor (computeGripBudgetFactor), stage 3 the committed chase vTarget = tan(committedSlip) * speed with an exponential response (computeNextLateralVelocity), stage 4 the countersteer authority (computeCountersteerAuthority), stage 5 the snap-back at the zero crossing (inside computeNextLateralVelocity), stage 6 the longitudinal speed scrub (computeLongitudinalSpeedScrub, owned by the service because the service owns speed), and stage 7 the merged pose spring (stepDriftPoseSpring); the two previous omissions (stage 2 and stage 6) are closed, so the packet and the implementation now agree'
      - 'the NAMED constant set is introduced with the RED-decided values: NEATRACING_DRIFT_MIN_SLIDE_PROXY_RAD (0.20 rad), NEATRACING_DRIFT_POSE_STEER_YAW_RAD (0.08 rad), NEATRACING_DRIFT_POSE_STIFFNESS_RAD_PER_S2 (324, omega 18 rad/s), NEATRACING_DRIFT_POSE_DAMPING_RAD_PER_S (12.6, zeta 0.35), NEATRACING_DRIFT_POSE_ARTICULATION_SLEW_PER_S (20, band 15-30), NEATRACING_DRIFT_POSE_STEER_YAW_FULL_SLIP_RAD (0.01), NEATRACING_DRIFT_STEER_ENGAGE_THRESHOLD (band 0.4-0.6), NEATRACING_DRIFT_STEER_NEUTRAL_THRESHOLD (band 0.1-0.2), NEATRACING_DRIFT_COUNTERSTEER_MIN_STEER (band 0.85-0.95), NEATRACING_DRIFT_COUNTERSTEER_HOLD_TICKS (band 6-10), NEATRACING_DRIFT_PROXY_ENGAGEMENT_MIN_RAD (0.01), NEATRACING_DRIFT_PROXY_MIN_FRAMES (3), and NEATRACING_DRIFT_MAX_SLIP_ANGLE_RAD moves from pi/2 to 0.45 rad; NEATRACING_DRIFT_GRIP_FALLOFF_THRESHOLD_RAD moves from 0.25 to 0.20 rad, because the re-based AC-079 argument DEPENDS on it - at the new max slip 0.45 the slip demand is 0.45 - 0.20 = 0.25 and the grip budget is 1/(1+2*0.25) = 0.667 < 0.7 (the 5 percent margin the artifact flags), while the old threshold 0.25 would give 1/(1+2*0.20) = 0.714 and BREAK that pin; the NEW named export NEATRACING_DRIFT_MIN_SPEED_DEFICIT_KMH is ADDED to the set in the SAME step (it is the one export the D1.3 replacement needs and it has no production caller until the fixture reads it): it is owned by THIS slice (drift.model.ts), its value is a RED decision that is MEASURED and never carried (the 127 km/h bleed of the old model at a 90 km/h entry and the about 4x deficit shrink under the new 10.0 m/s2 scrub are the artifact numbers, NOT a pin), the fixture MIRRORS it locally and the RED slice PINS the mirror against this export, and it ACCOMPANIES rather than replaces the re-pinned TRACTION_LOSS_MAX_SPEED_KMH ceiling, because the ceiling is a SPEED bound and this export is a SCRUB-RATE bound and the D1.3 check needs both'
      - 'the 3 NEW TYPES and the NEW FUNCTIONS of the merged contract are added: DriftCommittedState, DriftPoseSpringState and DriftChannelState, plus createZeroDriftChannelState, stepDriftCommitment, stepDriftPoseSpring, computeDriftSlideProxyRad and the re-homed computeCountersteerAuthority; the RE-ARM TOKEN gets a home in the ratified state shape - DriftCommittedState is {slip, turnSign, reArmed} (an A-8 AMENDMENT recorded by 01-planning: the ratified A-8 shape {slip, turnSign} had NO home for the RE-ARM token, and the token is REQUIRED by the engagement rule, so it is carried by the model state and never smuggled through a global); the turnSign is the TURN direction (+1 = LEFT) and NEVER sign(slip), and the ramp is committed.slip minus turnSign times ENTRY_RATE times |steer| times dt'

source_of_truth: 'plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md + the verdict5-merged-gap-map record at the plan tail + plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.research.md (Part B-1) + plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.research.md (Part B-2) + plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.research.md (Part B-3) + plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.research.md (Part B-4) + plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.research.md (Part B-5)'
copy_paste: true
next_step: 'Step 14Q - Drift re-wiring wave part 2: the PROPORTIONAL traction law + the PUBLISHED traction scalar (the law must exist before ANY traction is presented)'
pre_execute_hook:
  tool: 'neataptic-workflow-mcp-get_slice_context'
  args:
    slice_id: 'P1-drift-rewire-red'
skills:
  - implementation-standards
  - red-test-contracts
  - green-validation-gates
  - spec-checklist
validation:
  - 'npm run jest:base -- --testPathPatterns="examples/neatRacing/physics|examples/neatRacing/car|examples/neatRacing/host"'
  - 'npx jest --testPathPatterns=examples/neatRacing/browser-entry'
  - 'npx tsc -p tsconfig.neatRacing.json --noEmit'
  - 'npx eslint examples/neatRacing/browser-entry/chase-camera.ts examples/neatRacing/browser-entry/browser-entry.ts'
  - 'npm run build:neatRacing'
  - 'manual: npm run build:neatRacing + visible-window browser smoke on the served game page (the page boots in MANUAL mode; a sustained full-steer run at speed shows the road receding STRAIGHT UP the screen while the body crabs into the slide, and the served page is no longer an AI-driven grass car)'
  - 'manual: visible-window smoke fixture docs/browser-tests/scenarios/p1-turn-drift-green-smoke.html - window.p1TurnDriftGreenSmokeResult.passed === true and EVERY named check in result.checks is true; the check COUNT is ASSERTED against the ACTUAL result.checks length at green time and is NEVER assumed'
acceptance_criteria:
  - 'AC-087 (RE-DERIVED 2026-10-27, verdict-4 + verdict-5): the SEMANTICS are retained (a NAMED slide-prominence floor, the feel DIRECTION decided and RECORDED in this plan before any production edit, the user-approved body animation SHAPE retained, the sustained-slide contract). The NUMERIC PINS are re-derived: (1) the floor is still asserted on the DETERMINISTIC UNIT PROXY computeDriftSlideProxyRad (the browser reading stays a LOOSE PRESENCE observable and is NEVER compared numerically against the constant); (2) the slide DEPTH becomes SPEED-PROPORTIONAL - the OLD behaviour (the SAME 0.45 rad committed slide at 5 m/s and at 89 m/s, measured by the envelope audit) is the DEFECT, and the red contract pins the new depth law (the depth at the top speed at least 0.45 rad AND the depth at a low speed at most 0.20 rad; the exact split is a RED decision); (3) the sustained-slide window is measured on the ROAD in MANUAL mode (the off-road decel is 32:1 the drift scrub and pins an off-road car at 80.1 km/h, which masks the slide entirely); (4) the speed deficit is pinned at the EQUILIBRIUM 32.911 km/h and NEVER at a transient 600-tick reading; (5) the camera and the body read the SAME published slip, so the frame can never be internally inconsistent (a travel-locked camera with a crabbing body is the exact defect the audits forbid); (6) the 3D VIEW MOVES - a NEW red contract asserts the RENDERED camera basis actually translates on screen under a published slip, because the A1-A11 contracts and all 43 fixture checks can pass with a FROZEN camera.'
  - 'AC-089 (RE-DERIVED 2026-10-27, verdict-5): the PRESERVE SET is retained unchanged (AC-047A..AC-047D, the determinism twin-runs, the straight-line exact zeros, the low-speed exact-zero gate, AC-078 and its tyre-follow tolerance, the 24 non-drift fixture checks). The RE-BASELINED SET gains the rows this step legitimately invalidates, each with ONE ledger row (the pin, the old baseline, the new baseline, the measured value, the owner file) whose ONE home is THIS PLAN: the physics state shape (the state gains the travel direction field, so the AC-047D byte-identity is re-anchored on the PRODUCTION serializer at physics.step.service.test.ts, a STRONGER contract than the whole-object JSON.stringify pin), the DECLARED POSE ENVELOPE (re-derived from the PUBLISHED slip ceiling in the same slice that changes the body yaw source), the debug seam field count (5 to 6) and the fixture check count (43 to 44). NO SILENT DELETION, and the re-baselined green pins move in the SAME step as the production change.'
slices:
  - slice_id: 'P1-drift-rewire-red'
    title: 'Author the RED contracts for the travel direction on the state, the ONE aim law, the PROPORTIONAL camera follow and the 3D-VIEW motion (the core contracts of the re-wiring wave)'
    status: '[DONE] - the 8 RED contracts (RED-1..RED-8) are authored and every one is CONFIRMED RED; this slice authored NO production code. The red evidence is recorded in the 2026-10-27 PlanUpdate entry at the plan tail.'
    goal: red-testing
    estimate_hours: 4
    research_artifact: 'the verdict5-merged-gap-map record at the plan tail + plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.research.md (Part B-5) (G-M1..G-M12) + plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.research.md (Part B-4) (the wire ledger) + plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.research.md (Part B-2) (the numeric envelope)'
    files_to_change:
      - 'examples/neatRacing/physics/physics.step.service.test.ts'
      - 'examples/neatRacing/browser-entry/chase-camera.test.ts (NEW)'
      - 'examples/neatRacing/browser-entry/browser-entry.test.ts'
    acceptance_criteria:
      - id: 'RED-1 (the state contract - the travel direction)'
        text: 'physics.step.service.test.ts asserts that the physics state publishes the TRAVEL direction and that it is the physics own velocity heading: the new named field travelHeadingRad equals heading + published slip (wrapped), it is FINITE for every produced state, and it is EXACTLY the value the physics used to advance x and y (the velocityHeading the service computes at physics.step.service.ts:462 - the value that is today DISCARDED at :475, the G-M1 break line). The assertion reads the state field and NOT a re-derived local expression, so the test fails if the field and the integration ever diverge.'
      - id: 'RED-2 (the shared slip scalar and its sign)'
        text: 'physics.step.service.test.ts asserts that the PUBLISHED slip is the ONE shared scalar: the state field slipAngle is the published slip (the sign convention LEFT = negative slip is PINNED here, because the audits could not verify it), the pose spring is driven from that published slip and NOT from the committed slip, and a straight-line tick leaves the published slip EXACTLY 0. The G-V3 defect (the crab reads the committed slip while the traction law reads the published slip) is therefore closed by a contract, not by a comment.'
      - id: 'RED-3 (ONE aim law - the three call sites)'
        text: 'chase-camera.test.ts asserts that there is exactly ONE aim law: a single exported function returns the camera aim, and the three live call sites (the camera placement + the look target at browser-entry.ts:935-940 and :1010-1012, and the starfield yaw at :1000) all read that ONE function. The starfield yaw is asserted to equal carSceneYawRad(aim) and the pi/2 scene offset is RETAINED, so the sky never slides relative to the world during a drift.'
      - id: 'RED-4 (the 3D VIEW moves - the F3 trap)'
        text: 'chase-camera.test.ts asserts that the RENDERED camera basis ACTUALLY TRANSLATES under a published slip: with a non-zero published slip and the car heading held, the camera forward vector and the look target differ from the nose-aligned values by the travel divergence, so the scene translates on screen. The assertion is on the CAMERA BASIS (the look target and the forward vector), NEVER on the seam or on a channel value, because the A1-A11 contracts and all 43 fixture checks can pass with a FROZEN camera. The contract also asserts the CONVERSE: with a zero published slip the camera basis is BIT-IDENTICAL to the pre-wave basis (the straight-line identity).'
      - id: 'RED-5 (the PROPORTIONAL follow law - S-1 + S-4)'
        text: 'chase-camera.test.ts asserts that the camera follow is PROPORTIONAL and NOT a fixed time constant: the per-tick aim change is proportional to the SPEED times the shared drift amount (the user law S-1/S-4), so doubling the speed at the same slide roughly doubles the follow rate, and the follow is a slight ANIMATION with no snap (the per-tick change is bounded and the release is MONOTONIC toward the nose-aligned aim, with no overshoot and no discontinuity). The CONTESTED constants NEATRACING_CHASE_CAMERA_FOLLOW_TAU_S = 0.08 and NEATRACING_CHASE_CAMERA_TRAVEL_AIM_GAIN = 1 are REPLACED by S-1/S-4-conformant NAMED exports with a derived JSDoc, and the retired exports are DELETED in the slice that owns their file (no deferred cleanup).'
      - id: 'RED-6 (the dt is pinned)'
        text: 'chase-camera.test.ts asserts the frame-rate independence of the follow: the follow is stepped with the TICK dt (the 1/60 physics timestep, the buildComposerFrame frame builder is zero-arg and the follow is stepped inside the tick), so 60 ticks delivered as 1 x 60 and as 60 x 1 produce the IDENTICAL aim, and a zero-step frame holds the aim. The dt source is NAMED, not inlined.'
      - id: 'RED-7 (the signed wrap + the tick-regression reset)'
        text: 'chase-camera.test.ts asserts that a heading crossing plus or minus pi does NOT spin the camera by 2 pi (a shortest-path signed delta is used), and that a tick regression (a new car or a mode switch) resets the follow to the nose-aligned aim with NO stale offset. The reset has ONE named owner (the same idiom the wheel-spin accumulator uses at browser-entry.ts:942-946), so there is no second detector.'
      - id: 'RED-8 (the seam grows by exactly one field)'
        text: 'browser-entry.test.ts asserts that the browser drift seam carries EXACTLY SIX fields (the five live fields plus the new camera follow offset), that the assignment happens once per frame, and that the new field is the follow offset. The seam mechanics are RETAINED (one assignment per frame, no new public gameplay API) and the field count is asserted as an exact number, never as a range. The contract is authored in browser-entry.test.ts - the SEAM OWNER module test - and NOT in physics.step.service.test.ts, because the drift state type (NeatRacingDriftState, browser-entry.ts:131) is a MODULE-LOCAL, UNEXPORTED interface and the seam is assigned inside the ZERO-ARG buildComposerFrame closure (browser-entry.ts:931, the assignment at :980-986): the seam is therefore observable ONLY through the module own public window handle (window.neatRacingDriftState) after a frame is driven, and this slice FORBIDS the production export (a new public export would be a new public API and would break the one-assignment-per-frame seam rule). The assertion is made on the LIVE seam object, never on a re-derived local expression.'
    red_test:
      - 'RED-1 fails today because PhysicsCarState (physics.step.service.ts:78-130) carries the NOSE, a scalar slip and a lateral velocity and NO travel direction at all: the velocityHeading computed at :462 is used to advance x and y at :469 and :474 and is then DISCARDED at :475, so there is no field to read and the import of the named field cannot resolve.'
      - 'RED-2 fails today because the pose spring is fed with the COMMITTED slip (physics.step.service.ts:457 passes slipAngle: nextCommitted.slip), so the crab and the traction law read DIFFERENT slips (the G-V3 defect) and the published-slip sign is never asserted anywhere.'
      - 'RED-3 fails today because there is NO aim function at all: the camera placement and the look target are derived inline from car.heading (browser-entry.ts:935-940 and :1010-1012) while the starfield yaw copies the BODY yaw (:1000 <- carPoseBag.yawRad), so the two consumers can never agree and the module examples/neatRacing/browser-entry/chase-camera.ts does not exist.'
      - 'RED-4 fails today because the camera is a PURE STATELESS function of the NOSE: a published slip of 0.4502 rad (25.85 deg, measured) produces ZERO screen-space translation of the 25.85 deg off-axis travel, and no existing contract (A1-A11, and none of the 43 fixture checks) can detect a frozen camera.'
      - 'RED-5 fails today because there is no follow at all (the camera jumps), and the proposed constants NEATRACING_CHASE_CAMERA_FOLLOW_TAU_S = 0.08 and NEATRACING_CHASE_CAMERA_TRAVEL_AIM_GAIN = 1 are a FIXED time constant and a fixed gain - exactly the S-1 violation the user verdict named.'
      - 'RED-6 fails today because the camera has no dt-driven state at all, so there is nothing to be frame-rate independent; the named dt export does not exist.'
      - 'RED-7 fails today because the camera holds no state, so there is no wrap and no reset to assert; the named follow-state export does not exist.'
      - 'RED-8 fails today because the live seam at browser-entry.ts:980-986 carries EXACTLY FIVE fields (poseRad, slipAngleRad, speedMps, tickHz, tick) and there is no sixth. The contract is authored in browser-entry.test.ts (the SEAM OWNER module test) because the drift state type is module-local and unexported (browser-entry.ts:131) and the assignment happens inside the zero-arg buildComposerFrame closure - a contract in physics.step.service.test.ts could not observe the seam at all, and this slice is forbidden from exporting the type.'
    orchestrator_note: 'TESTS ONLY - no production file may be edited in this slice, and the three test files are the ONLY ones this step touches here (the slice is AT the 3-code-files cap: physics.step.service.test.ts + chase-camera.test.ts NEW + browser-entry.test.ts). Every on-disk test is UNVERIFIED input: re-run the three focused suites for ground truth and report the FAILING ASSERTION NAMES, so each RED fails for its OWN contract and NOT through a missing import that the whole module cannot load. The new module examples/neatRacing/browser-entry/chase-camera.ts does not exist yet, so the chase-camera.test.ts import failure is EXPECTED and must be reported as the contract failure - do NOT create a placeholder export to make the import resolve (the 14N import-fails form). The seam field-count contract (RED-8) is authored in browser-entry.test.ts and the seam is read through the public window handle after a frame is driven - NEVER by exporting the module-local NeatRacingDriftState type (the export is forbidden here and the one-assignment-per-frame rule must hold). Report the MEASURED current-model numbers this slice observes (the current published slip at a full-steer hold, the current travel divergence, the current screen-space translation) so the re-derived AC-087 pins are MEASURED and not carried.'
        red_contract_api: |
          THE RED CONTRACT API - this slice PINS the names the implementing
          slice must provide. The names below are the CONTRACT, not a
          suggestion: the green slice must export them VERBATIM.

          (1) examples/neatRacing/physics/physics.step.service.ts gains ONE
          named field on the car state:

              travelHeadingRad: number

          - it is the VELOCITY heading the service ALREADY computes at
            physics.step.service.ts:462 (`velocityHeading = nextHeading +
            nextSlipAngle`), the value it uses to advance x and y at :469 and
            :474 and then DISCARDS at :475 (the G-M1 break line);
          - the field is published, so the RED contract can read it off the
            state instead of re-deriving it;
          - the RED contract is WRAP-INVARIANT (it compares the wrapped
            values), so a wrapped [-pi, pi) publication and a raw publication
            are BOTH accepted;
          - the integration keeps using that EXACT value, so the published
            field and the x/y advance can never diverge.

          (2) examples/neatRacing/browser-entry/chase-camera.ts (NEW in the
          green slice) exports EXACTLY these names:

              NEATRACING_CHASE_CAMERA_FOLLOW_DT_S: number   // === 1/60
              NEATRACING_CHASE_CAMERA_BACK: number          // 5.5
              NEATRACING_CHASE_CAMERA_HEIGHT: number        // 2.4
              NEATRACING_CHASE_CAMERA_LOOKAHEAD: number     // 8
              createChaseCameraFollowState(): ChaseCameraFollowState
              resolveChaseCameraAimRad(headingRad, followOffsetRad): number
              stepChaseCameraFollow(follow, step): ChaseCameraFollowState
              resolveChaseCameraBasis(carX, carY, aimRad): ChaseCameraBasis

          - ChaseCameraFollowState carries EXACTLY two fields:
            { offsetRad: number, lastTick: number };
          - the AIM LAW: the camera aim is the NOSE heading plus the follow
            offset, and the follow offset is the SIGNED SHORTEST-PATH delta
            between the PUBLISHED travel heading and the nose heading;
          - stepChaseCameraFollow takes a step descriptor
            { ticks: number, headingRad: number, travelHeadingRad: number,
              speedMps: number, tick: number } and returns the NEXT follow
            state; `ticks: 0` HOLDS the aim; a tick REGRESSION
            (tick < follow.lastTick) resets offsetRad to EXACTLY 0;
          - the per-tick follow change is PROPORTIONAL to speedMps times the
            shared drift amount (the user law S-1/S-4), NOT a fixed time
            constant (the retired NEATRACING_CHASE_CAMERA_FOLLOW_TAU_S and
            NEATRACING_CHASE_CAMERA_TRAVEL_AIM_GAIN names are FORBIDDEN and
            must not exist);
          - resolveChaseCameraBasis returns
            { cameraWorld: [number, number, number],
              lookTarget: [number, number, number],
              forwardVector: [number, number, number] };
          - the camera placement, the look target and the starfield yaw in
            browser-entry.ts read that ONE aim law (RED-3), and
            NEATRACING_CAR_SCENE_YAW_OFFSET_RAD (pi/2) stays EXPORTED from
            browser-entry.ts with its current value.

          (3) the debug seam field name is PINNED:

              followOffsetRad

          - the seam (window.neatRacingDriftState) carries EXACTLY SIX
            fields: followOffsetRad, poseRad, slipAngleRad, speedMps, tick,
            tickHz. The count is an EXACT number, never a range.

          (4) the MEASURED current-model numbers (this slice; seed 42, road,
          dt = 1/60, full throttle, full LEFT steer = +1, 200-tick hold):
          - the drift ENGAGES at tick 52 (speed 15.42667 m/s, the 15 m/s
            MIN_SPEED gate): the published slip starts at -0.01772645 rad
            and the committed slip at -0.05833333 rad;
          - at tick 61: speed 18.04974 m/s, heading 0.203293 rad, PUBLISHED
            slip -0.34897859 rad, COMMITTED slip -0.45000000 rad, pose
            -0.20404854 rad, the published-slip spring reference
            -0.19950258 rad and the committed-slip spring reference
            -0.20404854 rad. The live pose EQUALS the committed-slip
            reference BIT-FOR-BIT (the G-V3 defect) and differs from the
            published-slip reference by 0.00454596 rad;
          - at tick 91: published -0.43154093, committed -0.45000000, pose
            -0.20330355, the published-slip reference -0.20247289;
          - the published-slip PEAK over the hold is -0.44354955 rad
            (25.41 deg) at tick 200 (speed 50.73673 m/s);
          - the TRAVEL DIVERGENCE equals the published slip (the velocity
            heading is the nose heading plus the published slip): at tick 61
            the advance was dx 0.2976422055 m and dy -0.0436715900 m, which
            is cos(heading + published) * speed * dt and
            sin(heading + published) * speed * dt EXACTLY;
          - the straight lane (steer 0) leaves the published slip EXACTLY 0
            at every tick (200 ticks, speed 59.333333 m/s);
          - the CURRENT screen-space translation is EXACTLY 0: the camera
            basis is a pure function of the NOSE heading, so the 0.4369 rad
            off-axis travel produces ZERO translation (the frozen-camera
            defect).

          (5) the PHYSICS red contracts (RED-1 and RED-2) are authored in
          examples/neatRacing/physics/physics.step.service.test.ts in the
          file's own style (AAA blocks, a nested describe per contract, and
          a LOCAL typed view for the not-yet-existing field so the file
          still COMPILES and each contract fails on its OWN assertion):
          - RED-1 reads the state field through a widened local view
            (`const travelHeadingRad = (state as unknown as {
            travelHeadingRad?: number }).travelHeadingRad;`), asserts it is
            a finite number, asserts it equals the WRAPPED
            `heading + slipAngle` (wrap-invariant, so a wrapped and a raw
            publication both pass), and asserts the x/y advance used EXACTLY
            that value (`result.x - state.x` equals
            `cos(travelHeadingRad) * result.speed * dt`, likewise for y, to a
            1e-12 tolerance);
          - RED-2 builds the PUBLISHED-slip spring reference
            `stepDriftPoseSpring(prev.drift.pose, { steer, speedPercent:
            clamp(prev.speed / NEATRACING_PHYSICS_MAX_SPEED_UNITS_PER_S),
            slipAngle: state.slipAngle, dt:
            NEATRACING_PHYSICS_FIXED_TIMESTEP_SECONDS })` and asserts the
            live `state.drift.pose.pose` EQUALS that reference (to 1e-12)
            and DIFFERS from the committed-slip reference (the same call
            with `slipAngle: state.drift.committed.slip`). The
            non-vacuity guard (the two references differ) is asserted
            FIRST, so the equality can never pass vacuously;
          - RED-2 also PINS the published-slip sign (a full LEFT steer, i.e.
            `steer: 1`, yields a NEGATIVE published slip) and the
            straight-line exact zero (a straight lane leaves the published
            slip EXACTLY 0);
          - the fixtures are the file's own: `createInitialPhysicsCarState
            (42)`, `FIXTURE_INPUT` (throttle 1, brake 0, steer 1 = LEFT),
            `STRAIGHT_INPUT` (steer 0), the road surface resolver and the
            200-tick hold. The drift ENGAGES at tick 52, so the pose
            discriminator is read at a tick INSIDE the slide (tick 61 or
            later).

          (6) the SEAM red contract (RED-8) is authored in
          examples/neatRacing/browser-entry/browser-entry.test.ts, in a NEW
          nested describe inside the existing boot-wiring describe (so it
          reuses the captured RAF callbacks and the boot doubles): the seam
          is read through the PUBLIC window handle
          (`(window as unknown as { neatRacingDriftState?: Record<string,
          unknown> }).neatRacingDriftState`) AFTER one driven frame, the
          field COUNT is asserted as the EXACT number 6, the field SET is
          asserted against the sorted list ['followOffsetRad', 'poseRad',
          'slipAngleRad', 'speedMps', 'tick', 'tickHz'], the new field is
          asserted to be a FINITE number, and the ONE-ASSIGNMENT-PER-FRAME
          mechanics are pinned with a window property accessor spy (the
          assignment site is a plain `window.neatRacingDriftState = {...}`
          write, so an accessor counts the writes: exactly one per driven
          frame). The module-local NeatRacingDriftState type is NEVER
          exported and NEVER referenced by name in the test.
        parallelizable: false
        dependencies: []

    status: '[DONE] - the travel direction is PUBLISHED on the car state, the body pose spring reads the PUBLISHED slip, the chase camera reads ONE aim law (the camera eye, the look target and the starfield yaw), the follow is PROPORTIONAL and stepped with the named tick dt, the debug seam grew 5 -> 6, and the targeted suites are GREEN (210/210). The implementing evidence is recorded in the 2026-10-27 PlanUpdate entry at the plan tail.'

**User instruction:** (2026-10-27 verdict-4 + verdict-5, relayed by the orchestrator — the driving still does not read as a drift and the camera is still wrong) — unwire the drift chain so the slide actually READS: the car must boot in manual mode and stay on the road while the drift is measured, the physics state must be able to say which way the car is actually travelling, and the camera plus the body must both be pointed at that travel direction instead of at the nose.

**Step objective:** Remove the two masks that make every drift measurement vacuous (the AI boot mode and the off-road excursion), publish the travel direction on the physics state, and re-point the camera and the body at the published slide through ONE aim law and ONE shared slip scalar, so that the rendered 3D view actually moves and the frame is internally consistent.

**Stop conditions:**

- **Done:** the physics|car|host lane and the browser-entry lane are green, neatRacing tsc is clean, the build passes, the fixture reports passed === true with every named check true, the seam carries six fields, the fixture carries 44 checks, the RE-BASELINE LEDGER rows are written with the MEASURED values, and the MANUAL-mode full-steer evidence is recorded.
- **Blocked:** the camera and the body cannot read the SAME published slip without a fourth code file in the travel/camera/body slice, or the surface classification cannot be exposed without re-deriving the Step 14I containment bound — record the blocker in Latest validation evidence and escalate via 00.cross-tier-helper; the slice MUST NOT be merged past the 3-file cap without a recorded decision.

**User instruction:** (2026-10-28 verdict-6, relayed by the orchestrator) — the car's weight at high speed must be what causes the drift when turning; a momentum law is critical and entirely missing today, and from playing the build the only thing that is noticed is an annoying camera effect.

**Step objective:** Make the drift a CONSEQUENCE of the momentum instead of a command from the wheel: the committed slide is produced by the momentum excess (the lateral acceleration the commanded turn demands minus the lateral acceleration the tires can hold at that speed), so the same wheel command slides deeper the faster the car goes, the slide is exactly zero at a standstill, and the old entry-rate command law is deleted in the same change that introduces the new one.

- **Blocked:** the momentum law cannot deepen the slide with the speed without breaching the depth budget, the severity bound or the PRESERVE SET — record the blocker in Latest validation evidence and escalate via 00.cross-tier-helper; the PRESERVE SET is NEVER relaxed, the severity bound is NEVER widened and the depth budget is NEVER raised to make a contract pass.

wave_note: 'AUTHORED 2026-10-28 by the 01-planning (AUTHOR) instance from the user_verdict_6 record at the plan tail (S-6: the turning rate must REDUCE slightly and PROPORTIONALLY to speed, never so much that it prevents turning or drifting, because it conveys the feeling of speed; S-7: AI agents may set the turn rate as a PERCENT which gives them full control, while the USER arrow inputs need a small speed-proportional turn-rate adjustment so the car becomes controllable and fun). This is the SECOND HALF of the verdict-6 wave SPLIT: wave part 4a (Step 14S) carries the MOMENTUM CAUSE (S-5) and this step carries the TURN-RATE laws. It runs AFTER Step 14S and AFTER the IN-FLIGHT Step 14R, which is NOT touched. THE SEAM WITH 14S IS THE DEMANDED TURN RATE: 14S made the DRIFT a function of the demanded turn rate; THIS step changes the demanded turn rate itself - so the two compose, and every pin the turn-rate change invalidates is re-pinned IN THIS STEP (the Step 14Q re-pin precedent: the re-pin lands in the SAME step as the production change that invalidated it, NEVER deferred). TWO SEPARATE LAWS ON THE SAME STEER AXIS (the verdict-6 status routing): the AI channel keeps FULL CONTROL by percent and is NEVER softened, while the user arrow channel gets the MILD speed-proportional adjustment - the two never collide, and the RED contracts assert the separation. THE AUTHOR DOES NOT DECIDE THE NUMERIC SPLIT: the RED slice MEASURES the mild band and the implementing slice implements the MEASURED value. PATCHED 2026-10-28 by the 01-planning (AUTHOR PATCH) instance per the 2026-10-28 verification patch list P-1..P-7: the RED contract TEXTS of the slice P1-turnrate-red were re-authored (the discriminating top-speed-versus-nominal clause moved into RED-1, RED-2 relabelled as a PRESERVATION GUARD, the two discriminating AI facts named in RED-4 and a 14Q-style NON-VACUITY GUARD opened on every relational lane), the stale source line citations were re-verified against the current tree, and NO status was flipped. NO green light is recorded here and NO execution is dispatched.'
